turns.tutor:
Sure. You know the basic rule: after he, she and it, the verb takes -s. The trickier part is spelling. Verbs ending in -sh, -ch, -s, -x or -o take -es (fix, fixes; go, goes), and a consonant plus y changes to -ies (study, studies). But a vowel plus y just adds -s (enjoy, enjoys). Also, "have" becomes "has".

Your task: write a short paragraph of three or four sentences about a friend's weekly routine. Try to include at least one -es verb, one -ies verb and one vowel-plus-y verb, using verbs of your own choice. I'll check each form.
